about: Whether a requirement's changed text changes what an implementer must DO. A tool cannot decide this, so the editor does, once, in writing. Keys are the requirement id and a hash of the text on each side, so a judgement made while drafting survives being re-run at release time against a tag.

baseline.why: The published release. Every diff is against this until 0.2 ships and becomes the new baseline.

R-A-002@c3d8b5dea7dc->6616fa3df605.why: Added an obligation that did not exist. The original said only when rowRef must be null; the revision also requires it to name the row in every other case. An implementation that emitted null everywhere satisfied the old text and fails the new one.

R-M-012@f9e12645b8b5->c749bb34ce1b.why: Two changes, both binding. Class 0,1 S / 0.1 was added to the permitted set, which relaxes the rule; and the record must now carry the standard and edition the class is claimed under, plus the meter serial and calibration date as before, which adds required fields. A conforming 0.1 record can be missing the edition.

R-C-013@6572965f993a->9d17150c7002.why: The obligation is unchanged: every message SHALL carry the common envelope. Only the illustrative JSON changed, from bpiVersion 0.1.0-draft to 0.2.0-draft, which follows the version bump rather than adding anything an implementer must do.

R-M-023@944813293552->cc57a9b312c6.why: The normative sentence is byte-identical -- efficiency SHALL name both endpoints and the path length, a bare figure is invalid. What changed is the italic rationale beneath it, which used to carry the efficiency-comparability argument withdrawn on 2026-08-24 and now carries the correction. See DISPOSITIONS C-1. No obligation moved.
